description: client.id in the ticket query schema accepts not_in (operators equals, in, not_in); a where clause `client.id not_in [ids]` validates and compiles
`client.id not_in` keeps tickets with no client and drops tickets whose client is listed; `client.id in` never matches a ticket with no client
Bundled view: `client.id not_in [A]` hides a bundle whose master or any child belongs to A; `in [A]` shows a bundle whose master or any child belongs to A
Checklist-template rule editor's Client field is pinned to equals/in, so a stored not_in Client rule is preserved as non-editable
checklistWhereForOwner simplifies `client.id not_in [owner]` to FALSE for an owned template and still throws for a foreign client id
TICKET_FILTERS_SCHEMA_VERSION is 3; the v2->v3 migration step moves a string clientId into where as `client.id in [clientId]` and deletes clientId
When where already has a client.id in/not_in clause, the v2->v3 step drops clientId and keeps the clause; the step is idempotent at v3 and never throws on odd input

Named views, board default views and the tenant default view holding clientId all open with the client row applied (via migrateListViewSettings, migrateTicketDefaultView and the ticketViewSettings read path)
URL entry points (server tickets page, container URL parser, parseReturnFilters) fold a legacy ?clientId= into the client.id where row using the same migration step
URL writers (getCurrentFiltersQuery, updateURLWithFilters) no longer emit clientId; the client row round-trips in the where parameter
ticketFiltersToPredicates still compiles filters.clientId for server callers but skips it when filters.where has a client.id in/not_in clause

WHERE_FILTERS has a Client row (path client.id, server-searched client options source, label fields.client, primary-row placement); chips, chip clear, isFiltered and the active-filter count derive from the table and the dashboard's separate client branches are removed
Client chips read `Client = <name>` / `Client ≠ <name>`, one per client, each removable on its own; an unresolved id shows a translated 'Unknown client' label, never the raw id
The Any of / None of mode button is one shared component used by WhereTagFilter, WhereLocationFilter and WhereClientFilter
WhereClientFilter replaces the single ClientPicker in the primary filter row: multi-select async client picker plus the mode button; toggling the mode keeps the selected clients and flips in/not_in
AsyncSearchableSelect supports a multi-select variant (values + onValuesChange): checks on selected rows, popover stays open on select, caller-supplied trigger label, Clear footer action

AsyncClientPicker supports multi selection (selectedClientIds, onSelectedClientIdsChange) with the existing status/type/tag header; trigger shows 'All Clients', the single name, or a '{{count}} clients' summary

A shared hook hydrates selected client names via searchClientsForPicker({ ids }) in one batched request per change, chunked at the 100-id lookup cap; used by the picker and the dashboard chips, replacing the single-id lookup
Contact filter options: Any of exactly one client -> that client's contacts including inactive; otherwise all active contacts narrowed to clients the row allows
Changing the client row clears the contact filter in the same update when the contact's client is not allowed by the new row (contactFilterUpdateForClientChange takes a row selection)
Location filter options are scoped to the client when the row is Any of exactly one client, tenant-wide otherwise
CSV export and adjacent-ticket navigation apply the client row (export filters carry where and stop setting clientId)
A named view (private, shared or per-user default) captured with a client row re-applies the same selection and mode and is not marked dirty
A client-portal user's own-client scope is never widened by a client.id where row
New UI strings (trigger summary, Unknown client, Clear) exist in every supported locale and pass validate-translations
